Definition: from G4862 and G1643; to drive together, i.e. (figuratively) exhort (to reconciliation):--+ set at one again.
BiblicalUsage: Moses comes to two Hebrews striving together and would have set them at one again, saying, Sirs, you are brethren, why do you wrong one another? The King James reading pictures Moses driving them together toward peace, though the older Greek copies read a different word for reconciling them there, and either way his plea is the same: brethren should not wrong brethren.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that peacemaking between brethren is God's work, and I hold that the plea still stands: Sirs, you are brethren, so why wrong one another?
